recognize_zh: 紅血球大小正常，但有些紅血球裡有多個細小環狀體（ring form），其中一顆裡有三個環，還看得到雙染色質點（double chromatin dot）和貼在紅血球邊緣的貼附型（appliqué form）；這些線索指向惡性瘧原蟲（P. falciparum）。
features: Multiple delicate ring-form trophozoites within normal-sized, non-enlarged RBCs
Multiply infected RBCs (one cell contains three rings)
Double chromatin dots and appliqué (accolé) forms at the RBC margin
Occasional slightly more mature trophozoite with denser cytoplasm and dark pigment
No Schüffner stippling; no schizonts or crescent gametocytes in this field
Background platelets adequate; one platelet clump in center
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous RBCs infected by small, delicate ring-form trophozoites. Infected RBCs are normal in size without stippling, and several contain two or three parasites, with double chromatin dots and appliqué forms at the cell margin. A few slightly more mature trophozoites with dark pigment are present; schizonts and gametocytes are not seen in this field. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum infection; parasitemia should be quantified.

ddx.vs: Infected RBCs are enlarged with Schüffner stippling and amoeboid trophozoites or schizonts, and multiply infected cells are uncommon.
Tiny pleomorphic rings without hemozoin pigment and tetrad (Maltese cross) forms, with a travel/tick history rather than malaria exposure.
Early rings can look identical, but band-form trophozoites and mature schizonts in circulation favor knowlesi, and PCR is needed to separate them.
A superimposed platelet lacks a ring of cytoplasm with a discrete chromatin dot and usually shows a halo and granular texture.
